chunks: Al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said:

When the people entered the religion in crowds, the Azd came to them as the softest of them in hearts and the sweetest of them in mouths. So it was said, 'O Messenger of Allah, this being the softest of them in hearts we have understood, but why did it become the sweetest of them in mouths?' He said, 'They used to use the siwak in the Age of Ignorance.'

key_terms.تَسْتَاكُ: used the siwak, a toothstick for cleaning the teeth

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith connect using siwak with sweetness of speech and good character?
ai.summary: This hadith relates that the tribe of al-Azd was distinguished by softness of heart and sweetness of speech. The Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم explained the latter quality by their habitual use of the siwak even before Islam, indicating the moral and social value of cleanliness and oral hygiene.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.115 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said :

"When people entered the religion in large numbers, the tribe of Azd came among them with the softest hearts and the sweetest mouths.
It was asked: 'O’ Messenger of Allah (sw), we understand why they have the softest hearts, but why do they have the sweetest mouths?'
He (sw) said: 'They used to use siwak (toothstick) even in the pre-Islamic period.'"
